candidate: Bounded direct native array construction plus synchronous array-item evaluation in this change
method: Each process checks nine fresh-interpreter runs and thirteen repetitions of one parsed program in one interpreter. First-five uses fresh[1:6], using the same warm-sample window as the earlier test, but not the same full protocol; fresh uses fresh[3:] and prepared uses prepared[3:]. Each comparison has twelve process pairs per selector form. Mac and final Intel comparisons alternate order. Intel replication is drawn from a balanced three-version rotation including an experimental candidate. Times exclude module loading and are milliseconds. Peak RSS includes module loading and is KiB. Paired ratios use geometric means of per-process median ratios. Bootstrap intervals resample process pairs, not individual warm samples: 10000 draws, seed 565. They describe these runs, not all machines or workloads.
memoryMethod: Five alternating process pairs for literal selectors with --expose-gc and gc mode. Explicit GC runs before every timed execution and after all executions. These timing samples are not used for the main speed comparison. retainedAfterGC describes the final live interpreter/program plus module state; peak RSS remains process-wide.
experiments: Only removing per-item generator wrappers did not produce a stable speedup. An eager general array constructor improved time but increased peak RSS. The final bounded direct constructor is faster on the exact original workload and preserves native validation and resumable fallback. Peak RSS still rises; retained JS heap after explicit GC is nearly unchanged.
extendedProtocolCaveat: gather-regression.mjs adds Rows and Columns bindings in both selector forms and constructs each Interpreter before starting its fresh-run timer. Its first-five window therefore does not exactly replicate array-selections.mjs. Results cannot be used to dismiss a slowdown in the unchanged original benchmark.
originalProtocolMethod: Unmodified benchmarks/array-selections.mjs ROOT gather: one cold execution and five fresh-interpreter warm executions per process, including Interpreter creation, parsing and preparation. Twelve balanced process groups per host rotate before/shipped/candidate order. This is the exact replication of the earlier gather workload.
